result: h07. **Where the URL comes from (before the image request):** the API never ships raw base64 avatars; `convertUserFromStore` rewrites `AvatarUrl` to `/file/users/{username}/avatar` when the stored value is a data URI — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:31-40` (with `BuildUserName` at `server/router/api/v1/user_resource_name.go:13`). The browser then puts that string into an `` in `web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:14`. **Hops for `GET /file/users/{username}/avatar`:** ``` — web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:12 FileServerService.RegisterRoutes (GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 (wired in server/server.go:81) FileServerService.serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 ├─ FileServerService.getCurrentUser — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708 (auth gate, only when !Profile.AllowAnonymous) │ └─ Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser — server/auth └─ FileServerService.getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148 (userCache is consulted only for ID lookups, so a username lookup always falls through) Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:136 Driver.ListUsers (interface) — store/driver.go:47 DB.ListUsers (SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (postgres/user.go:87, mysql/user.go:84) FileServerService.parseDataURI (base64-decode user.AvatarURL) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737 c.Blob(...) response — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:209 ``` Two things worth noting about this path: - The avatar bytes live **in the `user` row itself** as a base64 `data:` URI in `avatar_url` — not in the attachment/blob storage layer. So there is no local-file/S3 branch here, unlike `serveAttachmentFile`; the data layer is a single column read. - There is **no per-user authorization check** on another user's avatar. The only gate is instance-level: if `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` is false, *some* valid session/PAT is required (`fileserver.go:173-181`), but any authenticated viewer may fetch any user's avatar by username. That's deliberate — avatars are treated as public profile data — and contrasts with `checkAttachmentPermission` (`fileserver.go:650`), which does enforce creator/visibility rules.
